slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: Bringing on a partner, whether for capital, expertise, or shared workload, changes the business's financial structure, which is worth reviewing alongside the decision itself. Existing facilities and guarantees may need to be revisited.

slides.headline: Why it matters
bullet_points: Existing facilities may need to be reviewed or restructured
Personal guarantees can be affected by ownership changes
A partner may bring capital that changes finance needs
Clear documentation protects both parties from the outset

slides.headline: Key things to know
bullet_points: Engage legal and accounting advice alongside any finance review
Check whether existing lenders need to be notified
Consider how the partnership affects serviceability going forward
A broker can review your finance structure post-change

caption:
Bringing on a business partner is a significant decision on its own, and it's also a moment worth using to review the business's finance structure, existing facilities, personal guarantees, and serviceability can all be affected by a change in ownership.

Handling this proactively, alongside proper legal and accounting advice, avoids complications down the track.
